claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy in nanoscale thin-film or lithographically patterned nanoribbon form.
Pulsed laser deposition can be used to produce nanoscale alloy materials.
Pulsed laser deposition produces the specified FeMnNiGeSi thin films or patterned nanoribbons.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain inhomogeneous local strain and nanoscale heterogeneity.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit broad magnetocaloric transitions.
The as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit increased hysteresis because of distributed local strain and nanoscale microstructural disorder.
A controlled post-deposition anneal at 600°C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
Post-deposition thermal annealing relieves local stresses and reduces intrinsic nanoscale lattice strain in FeMnNiGeSi nanoribbons.
Annealing mitigates defect-induced domain-wall pinning associated with nanoscale heterogeneity.
Stress relief and increased microstructural uniformity decrease magnetic anisotropy caused by defect pinning.
Reduced pinning permits a more coherent magnetic phase transition.
A more coherent magnetic phase transition produces a sharper magnetic-entropy-change peak and reduced hysteresis.
Relative to the as-deposited control, annealed nanoribbons will show a narrower and higher magnetic entropy change peak.
Relative to the as-deposited control, annealed nanoribbons will show smaller hysteresis widths and lower cyclic magnetic loss.
The proposed effect is expected for films thinner than 10 nm or nanoribbons of comparable width.
The proposed effect is expected under applied magnetic fields below 1 T and near the magnetic transition temperature.
Intrinsic heat-transfer rates limit the attainable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Oxidation or diffusion during annealing may alter the magnitude of the magnetocaloric improvement.
A lack of statistically significant hysteresis narrowing and magnetic-entropy-peak sharpening or enhancement relative to an as-deposited control would falsify the proposed strain-relief mechanism.
